text:
A6 done, commit 853c003. `./gradlew assembleDebug lint test` green on the
first attempt: 0 lint errors, same 23 pre-existing version-freshness
warnings as A5 (deprecated hiltViewModel()/Icons.Filled.List usages show
up as kotlinc warnings, not lint findings — lint's ruleset here doesn't
flag them). 59 unit tests / 12 suites, all passing.

Design decision for future A7-A11 tickets that need drawer/logout/identity
access: reused LoginViewModel for the drawer instead of adding a new
ViewModel. It now takes a SessionState constructor param (breaking change
to its constructor — every existing test constructing LoginViewModel
directly needed a FakeSessionState() added) and exposes `loggedInEmail`.
AppDrawerScaffold changed from `private` to `internal` with an
overridable `loginViewModel: LoginViewModel = hiltViewModel()` default
param, same pattern LoginScreen already used for its own viewModel param
— this is what let AppDrawerScaffoldTest exercise the drawer standalone
(a minimal local NavHost with 3 dummy routes) without pulling in a full
Hilt test component. Any future ticket adding a testable Composable that
needs a ViewModel should follow this same "default = hiltViewModel(),
overridable for tests" pattern rather than reaching for Hilt test
infrastructure.

No emulator/AVD run for this ticket (consistent with A1-A5 precedent in
this project) — verification is Robolectric Compose tests only. Overview
screen's card-tap and FAB-create flows are covered by
OverviewViewModelTest against a real in-memory Room DB (not mocked), so
the create-list -> dirty -> (would-sync) path is genuinely exercised end
to end at the VM/repo layer, just not visually.

Infra note unrelated to app code: this sandbox is 4 cores / 3.7GB RAM.
Mid-build memory pressure (3GB+ swapped) was observed during this
ticket's build — the Gradle daemon, the separate Kotlin compile daemon,
KSP, and qemu-emulated AAPT2 (see app/build.gradle.kts's aapt2 override
note) can all peak concurrently, each defaulting to nproc-sized
parallelism / ~2GB heap ceilings. Added to android/gradle.properties:
org.gradle.workers.max=2 and kotlin.daemon.jvmargs=-Xmx1024m, and lowered
org.gradle.jvmargs from -Xmx2048m to -Xmx1536m. Future tickets' builds
should be noticeably less swap-prone; if thrashing recurs, the next lever
is Test.maxParallelForks (currently Gradle's default of 1, not yet
touched) or splitting assembleDebug/lint/test into separate gradlew
invocations instead of one combined command.
